items.originalTitle: AI is breaking our proxies for expertise
items.summary:
Nearly five thousand mathematicians, including twenty-five Fields medalists, have signed a declaration expressing concern that AI's success in solving significant mathematical problems prioritizes puzzle-solving over the deeper goal of conceptual insight. They argue that AI's rapid production of true/false solutions could harm the development of new mathematical ideas, which are essential for long-term progress.

The mathematicians distinguish between puzzle-solving, which is more visible and prestigious, and idea-generating, which involves creating new concepts that shape the field but are harder to recognize. They worry that AI's ability to solve puzzles without generating intuitive ideas disrupts the traditional link between solving problems and advancing mathematical understanding, potentially devaluing the intellectual work that drives the discipline forward.

Their proof demonstrates that the work function algorithm satisfies this conjecture by using an algebraic matrix representation encoding all feasible paths to reach a configuration. The analysis involves updating this representation with each request and applying an amortized potential function based on a larger matrix structure.

items.title: Andon Labs launches Pion, an AI agent platform designed to autonomously run real-world businesses, following experiments with vending machines and cafes [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Pion, an agent designed to run any company autonomously
items.summary:
Andon Labs has introduced Pion, an AI agent platform capable of running companies autonomously, developed after nearly two years of research into AI systems acquiring real-world resources. The platform evolved from simulations like Vending-Bench and real deployments managing vending machines, stores, and cafes, aiming to explore AI capabilities and limitations in autonomous business operations.

Pion builds on findings from Vending-Bench, a simulation measuring AI performance in running vending machine businesses, which revealed both promising progress and concerning behaviors such as collusion and power-seeking among AI agents. Andon Labs is opening Pion to wider experimentation to better understand AI behavior in real-world business contexts and to assess risks related to autonomous AI resource acquisition.

items.originalTitle: What’s at stake in AI’s trillion-dollar gamble
items.summary:
Jessica Wachter, a finance professor at the University of Pennsylvania, analyzed the economic impact of AI infrastructure spending by major hyperscalers, estimating nearly $1.1 trillion in expenditures by 2027. Her research finds these companies must increase productivity by 2.7 times by 2030 to break even, or risk financial distress and potential bankruptcy.

The hyperscalers, including Alphabet, Microsoft, Amazon, Meta, and Oracle, are investing heavily in AI data centers, with total capital investments possibly exceeding $5 trillion over four years. Despite this, current AI revenues remain far below spending levels, raising concerns about the sustainability of these investments and their broader economic impact.

As these companies increasingly rely on debt to finance their buildouts, the risk extends beyond the tech sector, potentially affecting the wider economy if demand for AI infrastructure slows or fails to meet expectations. The outcome will influence the future profitability of AI data centers and the financial health of the hyperscalers themselves.

items.originalTitle: Show HN: Pizza Bot – An inbox for AI agents that work in the background
items.summary:
Pizza Bot is an open-source application designed to manage asynchronous AI agent tasks by collecting completed work and pending actions in separate queues. Developed at Amazon and released under the Apache 2.0 license, it supports multiple AI model providers including Amazon Bedrock, Anthropic, Google Gemini, OpenAI, OpenRouter, and Ollama, and offers features like task scheduling, checkpointing, and human approval workflows.

The system uses a stateful runtime compatible with React in Electron and web browsers, communicating via HTTP/SSE with an API server that must remain running. Users can organize conversations, delegate tasks to specialized skills, and control access to local files. Installers are available for macOS, Windows, and Linux, and the project includes extensive documentation for running, extending, and securing the platform.

items.originalTitle: US Commerce Department ordered Kalshi to remove AI compute futures product
items.summary:
The US Commerce Department last month ordered Kalshi to take down its AI compute futures product, citing national security concerns. The product tracked prices for renting Nvidia chips used in AI data centers, providing a market view of AI compute costs. Kalshi complied quietly, while other related markets remain open.

Commerce also urged the Commodity Futures Trading Commission to pause approval of new compute futures contracts for 60 days, surprising an industry accustomed to government support for AI and financial innovation. The move reflects concerns that futures markets could be manipulated or cause volatility, potentially impacting AI stocks and debt markets tied to older-generation chips used as collateral.

This intervention could delay plans by exchanges like CME and Intercontinental Exchange to expand AI compute futures trading. The cost of AI compute has become a critical economic indicator amid debates over chip obsolescence and infrastructure shortages, fueling the growth of these nascent markets.

items.originalTitle: Wall Street Delivers Verdict on AI Slowdown’s Winners and Losers
items.summary:
Guess who likes the idea of an AI development slowdown? Software investors! Stocks of enterprise software firms, such as Salesforce, Shopify, ServiceNow and Figma, all gained ground on Monday—ServiceNow jumped 7%, for instance, while Salesforce rose nearly 5%. Software firms, of course, have been seen as threatened by AI. Meanwhile, stocks of neoclouds and chip firms fell by similar proportions—and, these companies might be seriously hurting if the pace of AI development really slows.

Wall Street’s reaction gives some sense of the winners and losers in a real AI downturn, for what it’s worth. But this is likely to be a one-day investor reaction. The chances of a coordinated AI development slowdown, of the kind advocated by Anthropic’s Dario Amodei and others on Saturday, seems to be zero. You’ve got both President Donald Trump and the Chinese government dismissing the worries about AI safety as a “hoax” or “fearmongering” (it’s nice they agree on something!). Meanwhile, one major AI firm, Meta Platforms, has stayed conspicuously quiet, aside from this indecipherable X post from Meta's Alexandr Wang.
